title: Sample-file mock presents fabricated documents as ready for extraction
repro: Sign in as an owner with an empty pipeline.
Open New order → AI Document Intake (Auto).
expected: Only files the user actually selected are shown, with their real status. Nothing is shown as provided, extracted or locked until the server has accepted it.
actual: Six invented files are listed (PO-8841_CustomerContract.pdf 248 KB 'Ready for extraction', SQ-4029_SupplierQuote.pdf 'Ready for extraction', Apex_DatedCashBalance.csv 'Deterministic parser ready', Payroll_AP_AR_Ledger.csv 'Decimal-safe parser active', WorkingCapital_TermSheet.json 'Structured terms locked', Owner_Risk_*).
resolution: Removed the fabricated intake path; the real API-backed order flow is the only path.

title: Validate step shows hard-coded Apex figures and computes profit and margin in the browser
expected: The validate step shows the user's entered values, with figures that come from the deterministic engine, never from browser arithmetic.
actual: Customer 'Apex Retailers Inc', Order Gross Revenue $360,000, costs $220,000, 'PROJECTED PROFIT +$140,000', 'GROSS MARGIN 38.9%' regardless of what the user entered. These values are computed in the browser.
resolution: Removed browser-generated validation figures; financial output is rendered from persisted engine results.

title: Fabricated order is shown as 'Audit Verified' on a fake deal id, from browser storage
expected: Submitting creates a saved order through the real API and shows the server's persisted id and evaluation state. Unsaved data is never labelled verified.
actual: The browser opens /deals/PO-8841/confirm, which shows 'Confirm Extracted Contract Terms', 'Audit Verified', GROSS REVENUE $360,000.00 and the same invented obligations. The network log has no POST to /deals; the page reads orderfit_deal_validated and orderfit_deal_draft from localStorage.
resolution: Removed the localStorage-backed confirmation screen and fake persisted reference.

title: Unknown URLs show an unbranded default Next 404 on a black page
expected: A branded not-found page with a header and a way back to the product.
actual: Page text is '404 / This page could not be found.' on a black background, with no navigation.
resolution: Added branded not-found, error, and global-error boundaries.

title: Signed-out visitors to a deal URL are told 'Your session expired'
expected: A visitor who was never signed in sees a plain sign-in prompt, not a session-expired message.
actual: 'Your session expired, so you were signed out. Sign in again; nothing was changed by the request that failed.'
resolution: Sign-in distinguishes a missing session from an expired session and preserves a safe return path.

title: KPI tile 'No loaded alerts' wraps into three cramped lines at desktop width
repro: Sign in and open Deals Pipeline with no orders.
expected: A stat tile with a short status value on one line, and a consistent type scale.
actual: 'No loaded alerts' is set at display size and breaks into 'No / loaded / alerts'. The tiles look inconsistent with the rest of the page.
resolution: Pipeline uses shared StatTile values and responsive grid sizing.

title: New-order intake cards crush their titles into the icon at 1024px
repro: Open /deals/new in AI Document Intake mode at 1024px.
expected: Card titles wrap below the icon or the grid reflows to fewer columns before text collides.
actual: '1. PURCHASE ORDER / CONTRACT' and '2. SUPPLIER QUOTATION' wrap next to the icon and overlap it.
resolution: The intake mock was removed; the real new-order form has responsive controls.

title: Empty pipeline table shows a horizontal scrollbar at 1024px
repro: Open Deals Pipeline with no orders at 1024px.
expected: No scrollbar when there is nothing to scroll.
actual: A horizontal scrollbar appears under the empty table.
resolution: The pipeline uses an empty state and cards below the table breakpoint.

title: Admin pages redirect to sign-in on any session error (per-page catch)
repro: Stop the API while on /admin/system and reload the page.
expected: A 'backend unavailable' state with a retry, the same as the admin layout's guard already shows.
actual: Not yet reproduced live; code shows a catch-all redirect to sign-in.
resolution: Admin layout is the sole guard and backend failures retain the current page with retry copy.

title: /orders is a circular stub that shows 'Loading…' with no content
expected: Either the orders list, or a redirect to /deals, with no misleading copy.
actual: The page says 'Saved orders are listed under Orders.' and links to /deals. Signed out, /orders redirects to sign-in; the stub copy is circular.
resolution: The legacy path redirects to the real deals pipeline.

title: Admin security page claims a tier table that the backend does not enforce as stated
repro: Compare the 'Step-Up Auth (SHA-256 Code)' and 'Owner / Admin MFA' rows with backend/orderfit/services and passkey code.
expected: Each tier row states what the system actually enforces (session-bound step-up with password or passkey, and no SHA-256 'code').
actual: Static copy describes a 'SHA-256 Code' step-up and 'Owner / Admin MFA'. Not yet reconciled with the implementation.
resolution: Admin security content now derives from the read-only capability model and avoids unsupported claims.
